chunks: Concerning a man who cut off the head of a dead person, he said: “The diyah is upon him, because his sanctity when dead is like his sanctity while he is alive.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: These reports also do not contradict what we have presented earlier, because in his statement, peace be upon him, “the diyah is upon him,” there is nothing explicit in their outward wording specifying the amount of that diyah, nor whether it is the diyah of a person or the diyah of a fetus. Since that is not stated in them, we interpret them to mean that in this case there is the diyah of a fetus, and the term diyah may be applied to that; and what indicates this is what he narrated:
And what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated, from Ibn Abī Najrān, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muskān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: concerning...

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام as the source of the report
key_terms.الدِّيَةُ: financial compensation legally due for bodily violation or injury
key_terms.الْمَيِّتِ: the deceased person whose body remains legally protected
key_terms.حُرْمَتَهُ: his inviolable sanctity and protected status
key_terms.دِيَةُ النَّفْسِ: the full blood-compensation of a human life
key_terms.دِيَةُ الْجَنِينِ: the compensation amount corresponding to a fetus

ai.seo_question: What diyah is due for cutting off the head of a dead person in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the legal ruling concerning one who mutilates the corpse of a deceased person by cutting off the head. It states that a diyah is due because the sanctity of the deceased remains protected after death, and then clarifies that the intended compensation is understood as the diyah of a fetus rather than the full diyah of a living person.
